title: Avatar
description: Avatars are found throughout material design with uses in everything from tables to dialog menus.

blocks.text: Image avatars can be created by passing standard `img` props `src` or `srcSet` to the component.

blocks.name: ImageAvatars

blocks.text: Avatars containing simple characters can be created by passing a string as `children`.

blocks.name: LetterAvatars

blocks.text:
You can use different background colors for the avatar.
The following demo generates the color based on the name of the person.

blocks.name: BackgroundLetterAvatars

blocks.text: You can change the size of the avatar with the `height` and `width` CSS properties.

blocks.name: SizeAvatars

blocks.text: Icon avatars are created by passing an icon as `children`.

blocks.name: IconAvatars

blocks.text: If you need square or rounded avatars, use the `variant` prop.

blocks.name: VariantAvatars

blocks.text:
If there is an error loading the avatar image, the component falls back to an alternative in the following order:

- the provided children
- the first letter of the `alt` text
- a generic avatar icon

blocks.name: FallbackAvatars

blocks.text: `AvatarGroup` renders its children as a stack. Use the `max` prop to limit the number of avatars.

blocks.name: GroupAvatars

blocks.text: If you need to control the total number of avatars not shown, you can use the `total` prop.

blocks.name: TotalAvatars

blocks.text:
Set the `renderSurplus` prop as a callback to customize the surplus avatar. The callback will receive the surplus number as an argument based on the children and the `max` prop, and should return a `React.ReactNode`.

The `renderSurplus` prop is useful when you need to render the surplus based on the data sent from the server.

blocks.name: CustomSurplusAvatars

blocks.text: You can change the spacing between avatars using the `spacing` prop. You can use one of the presets (`"medium"`, the default, or `"small"`) or set a custom numeric value.

blocks.name: Spacing
